recommendation: Keep the commit as-is. It clears stale core narrative after the replacement extension became available and after the later ServiceRequest.specimen removal was applied; no further core FHIR source change is needed for FHIR-48286.
issue_request: FHIR-48286 was Applied/Persuasive with Modification for R6. Although the original request asked to remove ServiceRequest.specimen, the approved OO disposition was to address the concern through FHIR-34206 by deprecating ServiceRequest.specimen, preferring Specimen.request for normal specimen-to-order linkage, and using a replacement specimenSuggestion extension for requester-side specimen suggestions; a later comment clarified that the disposition was deprecation, not immediate removal.
initial_application: Commit dda946573613133578cca95aed78dd03bc374351 deprecated ServiceRequest.specimen and added replacement guidance for FHIR-34206/FHIR-48286. Commit b0b8b0e63dc489546525c1e5b1a9e35a1aab11ae corrected the replacement extension name and added a temporary balloter note saying servicerequest-specimenSuggestion was expected soon. The Extension Pack later added the extension in PR #197, and the combined branch already contains the FHIR-50611 notes-link cleanup and the FHIR-55444 audit of PR #4006's ServiceRequest.specimen removal.
additional_context: ServiceRequest is active current-build source in source/fhir.ini. The FHIR Extension Pack checkout contains an active servicerequest-specimenSuggestion StructureDefinition, and current ServiceRequest notes link to it. FHIR-54625 was later Resolved - No Change because ServiceRequest.specimen no longer exists, confirming that the old two-way conflict is gone. The remaining core-source defect was the stale introductory note that still described the replacement extension as pending.
reconciliation: Removed the obsolete Note to Balloters block from source/servicerequest/servicerequest-introduction.xml. The edit leaves the ServiceRequest notes replacement guidance intact, does not reintroduce ServiceRequest.specimen, and relies on the Extension Pack as the source of truth for the extension.
